svg.title: An Execution-Only Barrier Is Not a Memory Barrier
svg.desc: Broken and fixed two-wave timelines show how an unfenced LDS write can pass an execution-only barrier, corrupt a reduction, and desynchronize pseudorandom draws. An ISA audit, instruction cost, and paired performance bars quantify the fix.
svg.text: An Execution-Only Barrier Is Not a Memory Barrier
s_barrier on AMDGCN is IntrNoMem — it orders waves, not memory
s_barrier alone is execution-only — LLVM models it IntrNoMem.
The pre-fix kernel has 49 barriers behind waits
emitted for unrelated reasons: accidentally correct,
not correct by construction. Post-fix, in flight is
zero — the property that actually matters.
the fix costs the register tier nothing.
the specializer is selected for all six circuits
The fence restores the reduction before selection, so
both backends consume the same PRNG stream for the shot.
The gate caught it. It was diagnosed for months as an FP-rounding problem in the noise ops — it was a missing fence.
